RBI Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) Operating Framework
Reserve Bank of India Monetary Policy Committee Operating Framework: The policy repo rate under the Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF) serves as the anchor rate for money market interest rates. The Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) rate operates at repo rate minus 25 bps (6.25% when repo is 6.50%), and the Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) operates at repo rate plus 25 bps (6.75%). The MPC targets medium-term consumer price index (CPI) headline inflation of 4.0% within a +/- 2.0% tolerance band.

findings.executive_thesis:
Strategic Recommendation: HOLD. Conviction 20/100. Target corridor INR 175-200. Stop-loss floor INR 168. Sequential architecture analysis indicates the asset is currently oversold but lacks fundamental catalysts for immediate mean reversion.

Quantitative & Order Flow Edge: RSI at 23.6 signals extreme oversold conditions, yet 47.4% annualized volatility necessitates caution. Corwin-Schultz spread of 175 bps reflects high transaction costs. Derivatives data (PCR 0.95, ATM IV 16.5%) suggests neutral sentiment near the INR 180 Max Pain level. Institutional execution mandates VWAP over 30-minute intervals to mitigate liquidity impact.

Corporate Performance & Macro Policy: Quarterly revenue of INR 3,601.50 Cr is offset by a net loss of INR 625.50 Cr, yielding a -17.37% margin and -27.05% ROE. SEBI LODR compliance is clean. RBI repo rate stability at 6.50% and CPI at 5.49% provide a predictable cost of capital environment, though this fails to offset the underlying operational cash burn.

Adversarial Bounds & Capital Preservation: Stress testing confirms resilience to a 2x volatility shock, with a 99% VaR of 13.90% remaining within the 15% threshold. However, the strategy fails the statutory drag test; the current annualized return profile cannot sustainably absorb the 22.22 bps roundtrip friction. Capital preservation remains the primary concern until operational profitability improves.
